findings.title: Team admins and owners are incorrectly required to hold both roles
findings.body: This permission check combines `isTeamAdmin` and `isTeamOwner` with `&&`, so a user who is only an admin or only an owner is denied access. The booking UI and variable name treat these as alternative roles; use an OR check so either authorized role can add guests.

findings.title: Email comparisons allow case-variant duplicates and blacklist bypass
findings.body: Guest addresses are compared verbatim against existing attendees and against a blacklist whose entries were lowercased. Since email addresses are case-insensitive, a differently cased address can bypass the blacklist and can be added again as a duplicate attendee. Normalize addresses consistently before filtering and persistence.

findings.title: Calendar attendee updates use the requesting user's credentials
findings.body: This endpoint explicitly permits attendees and team admins to add guests, but it loads credentials from `ctx.user` and uses them to update the booking's calendar attendees. For a non-organizer requester, those credentials may not own or have access to the organizer's calendar, so the update can fail or leave the calendar unchanged even though the database attendee list was already modified. Use credentials that can update the booking's calendar, or avoid attempting that update when the requester cannot do so.

findings.title: A calendar update failure leaves the booking changed while the request fails
findings.body: The attendee records are committed at line 92 before this external calendar update. If the calendar operation throws, the mutation returns an error even though the guests were added; the notification step is then skipped, and retrying the same guests can fail because they now exist. Handle this partial-success case explicitly, such as by reporting the committed result and retrying calendar/email side effects separately.

findings.title: Guest-add notifications ignore disabled standard email settings
findings.body: Unlike the existing location-change and scheduling email senders, this function sends organizer and attendee notifications without checking the event type's `disableStandardEmails` settings. Adding guests therefore still emails recipients for event types configured to disable standard host or attendee emails. Pass the event type metadata into this sender and honor the corresponding settings.
